answer: Each agent parks a refundable bond at a public vertex registry before peers will attest its work. With the bond it publishes a relic: a one-time registrar-signed token bound to its key and this epoch. Honest nodes refuse any answer whose relic is missing, spent, or absent from the live board. When a tide of look-alike keys reuses a relic or collides on the same registrar nonce, peers post a slash receipt; a quorum burns the bond and blacklists the cluster. Forging many identities therefore costs a full bond plus a unique relic each, enforced by a board lookup and a majority slash.
